party_summary: Growlithe / Pachirisu / Timburr / Hoothoot / Corphish / Treecko - Route101/102/103 wilds plus one C01 starter, nothing evolved, no legend.

driver.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, native AI and native debug battle lifecycle. Not earned campaign play.

attempts.narrative: T1 I spent the turn on the declared Lightning Rod probe: Growlithe Protected while Pachirisu aimed Nuzzle at PARAS, and the engine redirected it to Pikachu, which absorbed it for +1 Sp.Atk - the check E0001 could never run. Pikachu's Volt Tackle and Paras' Leech Life both hit the Protect. T2 Pachirisu's Follow Me pulled Pikachu's Volt Tackle onto a Volt Absorb body ('it doesn't affect Pachirisu'), and Growlithe's Close Combat removed Pikachu. Mienfoo replaced it. T3 Pachirisu withdrew for Timburr; Growlithe Protected again and Paras finally selected Spore, which the guard blocked. T4 Mienfoo's Drain Punch took Growlithe from 43 to 1 through its own Close Combat defence drops; Flare Blitz burned Mienfoo and Timburr's first Rock Slide killed it and flinched Paras. Bunnelby replaced it. T5 Growlithe withdrew for Hoothoot; a critical Rock Slide took Paras to 10 and Bunnelby to 21. T6 Paras Protected a 4x lethal Air Slash while Mach Punch removed Bunnelby. T7 Air Slash finished Paras. 4-0, no player faints, but Growlithe finished on 1 HP and Hoothoot on 6.

strategy_checks.check: Lightning Rod redirects a single-target Electric move aimed at its partner
strategy_checks.evidence: T1. Pachirisu's Nuzzle was declared at battler 3 (Paras) and the log reads 'The opposing Pikachu took the attack! The opposing Pikachu's Sp.Atk rose!' Redirection and the Lightning Rod boost both fired correctly. This clears the check that went untested in E0001 across two passes.

strategy_checks.check: Paras lands Spore on a legal, powder-vulnerable target
strategy_checks.evidence: T3 Paras chose Spore on Growlithe; Growlithe's Protect blocked it. The AI could not have known about the guard, so the selection is the thing being tested and it fired. This is a real behavioural difference from E0001's Shroomish, which had the same move and never chose it once in six turns across two passes - so Spore is selectable, and the E0001 omission is a scoring problem specific to that board, not a blanket 'sleep is never chosen'.

strategy_checks.check: Paras selects Wide Guard against real spread pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Never selected, in seven turns. The T4 Rock Slide is excusable (first use, unseen). The T5 one is not: Timburr had used Rock Slide the previous turn from the same slot, Paras was at 31/49 with a partner at 39/39, and Wide Guard would have blocked the spread that then critically hit Paras for 21 and Bunnelby for 18. Paras instead chose Leech Life into Hoothoot, which resists Bug. Wide Guard has never fired for this trainer in either pass.

strategy_checks.check: Paras does not automatically shield both supports; it attacks or repositions on turn two
strategy_checks.evidence: It attacked on T1, T4 and T5 and guarded only once, on T6, when the guard was lethal-denying. No reflexive double-shielding.

strategy_checks.check: Mienfoo supplies Fake Out while Paras acts, or pressures with Drain Punch/Knock Off
strategy_checks.evidence: Mienfoo entered as a replacement at the end of T2 and had a legal Fake Out turn on T3; it chose Drain Punch both turns instead. Defensible - the T4 Drain Punch took Growlithe from 43 to 1 and was worth far more than a flinch - but the authored Fake Out never fired and neither did U-turn, so the Regenerator pivot identity the plan describes went unexercised.

strategy_checks.check: Regenerator is credited only when a switch actually occurs
strategy_checks.evidence: Mienfoo never switched, so no phantom Regenerator recovery occurred.

strategy_checks.check: Pikachu uses Fake Out only when interruption is needed
strategy_checks.evidence: Pikachu never used Fake Out; it chose Volt Tackle both turns. Given a Protect turn and then a Follow Me turn, neither choice converted, but the selection logic did not default to a reflexive Fake Out.

protect_ledger.payoff: Blocked an Air Slash that was 4x super effective on Bug/Grass and lethal from 10 HP. Large payoff - it bought Paras a seventh turn.

protect_ledger_note: One opponent Protect in seven turns, and it denied a certain KO. Pikachu also carries Protect and never used it, including on the turn it threw Volt Tackle into my Protect and the turn it threw Volt Tackle into a Volt Absorb immunity.

ai_defects.board: Paras 31/49 with Wide Guard, partner Bunnelby 39/39, opposite Timburr which had used Rock Slide from the same slot on the previous turn.
ai_defects.chosen: Leech Life on Hoothoot (Normal/Flying, which resists Bug)
ai_defects.better: Wide Guard. It blocks the Rock Slide that in fact critically hit Paras for 21 and Bunnelby for 18, i.e. ~39 damage across the side, for a move that cost nothing.
ai_defects.status: STILL PRESENT. Wide Guard has not fired for Allen in either pass.

ai_defects.board: Huge Power Bunnelby (Attack 74 after Huge Power, no Intimidate on it) opposite Hoothoot, which is slower than Bunnelby (28 versus 34) and was at 22/50 on T6.
ai_defects.better: Frustration. At friendship 0 it is 102 BP with STAB against a target that has no Flying resistance to Normal and is already outsped, so priority buys nothing. Frustration kills the 22 HP Hoothoot on T6 outright; Quick Attack left it on 6 and it then finished the battle. Rock Slide, super effective on Hoothoot, was also available.
ai_defects.status: NEWLY OBSERVED in this pass (Bunnelby never reached the field in the previous receipt's run). This is the low-power-priority-over-lethal-attack failure, and it is the mirror image of the setup-pricing problem: here a cheap move wins scoring against the move that actually ends the turn.

ai_defects.board: Paras with Leech Life opposite Fire-type Growlithe (T1, T4) and Normal/Flying Hoothoot (T5) - both resist Bug 0.5x - while a neutral Pachirisu or Timburr was in the other slot on T1 and T5.
ai_defects.chosen: Leech Life into the resisting target, three times
ai_defects.better: Leech Life into the neutral slot, or Spore, or Wide Guard. The three Leech Lives dealt roughly 9, 9 and 21 across the fight.
ai_defects.status: Contributory rather than decisive, but it is the same family as D1: the AI keeps choosing a weak damage roll over a support move that is worth more.

ai_defects_newly_introduced: E0004-D2 (Bunnelby preferring Quick Attack to a lethal Frustration). Not previously observed because Bunnelby never entered the field in the first pass, so it cannot be attributed with confidence to the new pricing - but it is a live, reproducible mis-selection today.
ai_improvements_observed: Spore was selected (T3). The setup/support pricing does reach sleep on at least some boards.
Zero voluntary opponent switches; no free pivot faints.
level_change_reason: Won on attempt 1 with zero player faints. The +1 goes on the two lowest-offset, least-effective members: Pikachu spent both its turns throwing Volt Tackle into a Protect and then into a Volt Absorb immunity and died on T2, and Mienfoo landed one good Drain Punch and died on T4. Paras (offset 3) was the team's real engine and keeps its level; Bunnelby's poor showing is the AI defect D2, not its level, so it also keeps. Cumulative across both passes: Pikachu +1, Mienfoo +1 - well inside the +-2 cap, and the first pass made no change here at all.
cooler: Yes. Bunnelby's Frustration-at-friendship-zero is a lovely piece of authoring that the AI actively refuses to use, and Quick Attack is the move stealing its turns. Replacing Quick Attack with Fake Out would give the Huge Power slot a disruption turn on entry that does not compete with Frustration for the same job, and would preserve the priority identity without the AI being able to pick a 40 BP filler over a 102 BP STAB. Recording only - no change in this pass.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. Bunnelby's friendship=0 materialized correctly (Frustration was legal and selectable).
